metadata.name: Retail
metadata.description: Two years of real invoice lines from a UK online gift wholesaler: customers, products, sales, cancellations and returns, with modeled payments and customer segment history.

source.publisher: Daqing Chen, UCI Machine Learning Repository
source.release: Online Retail II (2019), worksheets Year 2009-2010 and Year 2010-2011
source.attribution: Chen, D. (2012). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Modified by Runtime.
transformations: All invoice lines for a deterministic 14% sample of customers (FNV-1a hash of customer id) and the same share of anonymous invoices, Dec 2009 – Dec 2011.
Overlapping worksheet dates (2010-12-01..09) are taken once, from the second worksheet.
One order header per invoice number (earliest line timestamp); order_type from the invoice prefix.
Product catalog covers every stock code in the full source; description and list price are the modal recorded values.
Categories are derived from product descriptions; products with no description stay uncategorised.
returns links each cancellation line to the latest earlier sale of that code to that customer.
customer_history derives segment from trailing-12-month net sales at each month start.
payments are modeled by Runtime (seed 20251): the source contains no payment ledger.

reproduction.command: node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> retail && node datasets/acquire/retail.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs retail
reproduction.notes: Committed extracts in datasets/retail/extract are the build input; the acquisition script regenerates them from the pinned source file.

tables.name: categories
tables.grain: One product category (for example Christmas or Kitchen). Products are grouped into these from their descriptions.

columns.name: department
columns.meaning: Broader group of categories; Non-merchandise covers fees and accounting adjustments

tables.name: products
tables.grain: One product in the catalog (one stock code). Some products never appear on invoices in this sample.

columns.name: stock_code
columns.meaning: Product code; letter codes often mark fees, samples, or adjustments

columns.name: description
columns.meaning: Usual product name; NULL if the source never described this code

columns.name: category_id
columns.meaning: Category for this product; NULL if it has no description

columns.name: list_price
columns.meaning: Typical sale price in GBP; NULL if never sold at a positive price

columns.name: first_sold_at
columns.meaning: First time this product appeared on any invoice

columns.name: is_merchandise
columns.meaning: 1 for goods, 0 for postage, fees, samples, and adjustments

tables.name: customers
tables.grain: One known customer. Anonymous (walk-in) invoices have no matching customer row.

columns.name: country
columns.meaning: Country on the customer’s first invoice

columns.name: region
columns.meaning: United Kingdom, Europe, or Rest of World

columns.name: first_order_at
columns.meaning: Time of the customer’s first invoice

tables.name: orders
tables.grain: One invoice: a sale, a cancellation (credit note), or an accounting adjustment.

columns.name: invoice_no
columns.meaning: Source invoice number; C = cancellation, A = adjustment

tables.name: order_items
tables.grain: One line on an invoice. Cancellation lines use negative quantities.

columns.name: line_number
columns.meaning: Position on the invoice, starting at 1

columns.name: description
columns.meaning: Text printed on this line; can differ from the catalog name

columns.name: quantity
columns.meaning: Units sold; negative on cancellations and stock adjustments

tables.name: payments
tables.grain: One payment attempt for a sale invoice. Payments are modeled; the original source has no payment ledger.

columns.name: status
columns.meaning: captured or failed; only captured attempts count as paid

tables.name: returns
tables.grain: One cancelled invoice line, linked to the earlier sale it reverses when that sale is in the data.

columns.name: original_order_id
columns.meaning: Earlier sale of the same product to the same customer; NULL if none is found

columns.name: returned_at
columns.meaning: When the cancellation invoice was issued

tables.name: customer_history
tables.grain: One version of a customer’s segment and country over time. A new row starts when either changes.

columns.name: segment
columns.meaning: occasional, regular, or key_account based on recent net sales

columns.name: valid_to
columns.meaning: First date it no longer applies; NULL if this is the current version

columns.name: is_current
columns.meaning: 1 if this is the customer’s current version

edgeCases: Cancellation invoices with negative quantities
Anonymous invoices without a customer
Repeated identical invoice lines
Zero-price adjustment lines and non-merchandise codes (postage, fees, samples)
Products never bought by the sampled customers
Undescribed products with no category
Returns with no matching earlier sale
Unpaid sale invoices, failed attempts and split payments
Customers whose segment or country changes over time
qualityNotes: Net sales are quantity × unit_price summed over sale and cancellation lines; payments are a separate modeled ledger.
Timestamps are recorded local times with an unspecified time zone.
A 14% customer sample is not a full-company total; compare shares and trends, not absolute company revenue.
Line descriptions can differ from catalog descriptions for the same stock code.

checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(ordered_at, 1, 7)) FROM orders

checks.name: countries
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT country) FROM orders

checks.name: cancellation orders

checks.name: anonymous orders

checks.name: repeated identical lines
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id, stock_code, quantity, unit_price HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

checks.name: products never bought in sample
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items i WHERE i.stock_code = p.stock_code)

checks.name: uncategorised products

checks.name: categories in use
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category_id) FROM products

checks.name: unpaid sale orders
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE order_type = 'sale' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.order_id AND p.status = 'captured')

checks.name: failed payment attempts

checks.name: split-paid orders

checks.name: returns linked to a sale

checks.name: returns without an earlier sale

checks.name: customers with history changes

checks.name: one current version per customer

metadata.name: U.S. Flights
metadata.description: Every domestic flight flown by a sample of 435 aircraft in January–March 2025: schedules, delays, cancellations, diversions and delay causes.

source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics; OurAirports
source.release: Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present), January–March 2025; OurAirports airports.csv retrieved 2026-10-14
source.license: U.S. government work (public domain); OurAirports data is public domain
source.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance. Airport names and coordinates: OurAirports (ourairports.com). Modified by Runtime.
transformations: All flights of a deterministic 7.5% sample of aircraft (FNV-1a hash of tail number); flights without a tail number sampled by carrier, flight number and date.
Selected 25 of 110 source fields; diversion detail fields are omitted.
Clock times combined with the flight date; actual times are scheduled time plus reported delay minutes.
Scheduled arrival date chosen so local arrival is closest to departure plus scheduled elapsed time.
Airport names and coordinates joined from OurAirports by IATA code; carrier names and groups added by Runtime.

reproduction.command: node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> flights && node datasets/acquire/flights.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs flights
reproduction.notes: Committed extracts in datasets/flights/extract are the build input.

tables.name: airlines
tables.grain: One airline.

tables.name: airports
tables.grain: One airport that appears in this dataset.

tables.name: routes
tables.grain: One flight path from an origin airport to a destination airport.

columns.name: distance_miles
columns.meaning: Distance between the airports in miles

tables.name: calendar
tables.grain: One calendar date in the first quarter of 2025.

tables.name: cancellation_reasons
tables.grain: One reason a flight can be cancelled (for example weather or carrier).

tables.name: flights
tables.grain: One scheduled domestic flight, including cancelled and diverted flights.

columns.name: tail_number
columns.meaning: Aircraft ID; NULL when not reported

columns.name: route_id
columns.meaning: Route for this origin and destination

columns.name: scheduled_departure
columns.meaning: Scheduled departure time at the origin

columns.name: actual_departure
columns.meaning: Actual departure time; NULL if cancelled

columns.name: departure_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes late leaving (negative = early); NULL if cancelled

columns.name: taxi_out_minutes
columns.meaning: Minutes from leaving the gate to takeoff

columns.name: scheduled_arrival
columns.meaning: Scheduled arrival time at the destination

columns.name: actual_arrival
columns.meaning: Actual arrival time; NULL if cancelled or diverted

columns.name: arrival_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes late arriving (negative = early); NULL if cancelled or diverted

columns.name: diverted
columns.meaning: 1 if the flight landed somewhere other than its destination

columns.name: carrier_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes of delay blamed on the airline (only when arrival delay is 15+ minutes)

columns.name: weather_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes of delay blamed on weather

columns.name: nas_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes of delay blamed on air traffic control

columns.name: security_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes of delay blamed on security

columns.name: late_aircraft_delay
columns.meaning: Minutes of delay from a late incoming aircraft

edgeCases: Cancelled flights with NULL actual times and delays
Diverted flights with a departure but no arrival delay
Early departures and arrivals (negative delays)
Overnight flights arriving the next calendar day
Local times in different time zones at origin and destination
Delay causes reported only for arrivals 15+ minutes late
Flights without a reported tail number
Holidays and weekends in the calendar
qualityNotes: Times are local; subtracting departure from arrival across time zones does not give duration. Use air_time_minutes.
A cancelled flight has unknown delay, not zero delay.
The sample is of aircraft, so carrier shares reflect the sampled fleet as well as schedules.

checks.name: flight dates covered
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT flight_date) FROM flights

checks.name: aircraft (tail numbers)
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tail_number) FROM flights

checks.name: largest origin share
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM flights GROUP BY origin)

checks.name: cancelled flights
checks.sql: SELECT SUM(cancelled) FROM flights

checks.name: diverted flights
checks.sql: SELECT SUM(diverted) FROM flights

checks.name: cancelled flights have no delay
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE cancelled = 1 AND departure_delay IS NOT NULL

checks.name: early departures
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE departure_delay < 0

checks.name: overnight arrivals
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE substr(scheduled_arrival, 1, 10) > flight_date

checks.name: cancellation reasons used
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cancellation_code) FROM flights

checks.name: flights with delay causes
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE carrier_delay IS NOT NULL

checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM airports WHERE latitude IS NULL

metadata.name: Product / SaaS Analytics
metadata.description: Eighteen months of a fictional collaboration product: workspaces, users, invitations, projects, sessions, raw event deliveries, experiments, plan changes and billing.

transformations: Workspace fit drives activation, team growth, session frequency, upgrades and churn; exceptions are sampled, not removed.
Five of twenty experiments carry a real effect on their primary metric; one has an intentional 55/45 allocation; one has three arms.
About 2.5% of client events are retried (repeated event_id), 4% arrive minutes to hours late and 1% arrive days late.
About 1.2% of project creations have no project_created event (tracking loss).

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

tables.name: accounts
tables.grain: One customer workspace (a company or team).

tables.name: users
tables.grain: One person in one workspace.

columns.name: referred_by_user_id
columns.meaning: User in another workspace who referred this workspace creator; NULL otherwise

columns.name: deactivated_at
columns.meaning: When an admin removed the user; NULL if still active

tables.name: subscriptions
tables.grain: One plan period for a workspace. Each workspace has exactly one current plan (no end date).

columns.name: billing_period
columns.meaning: monthly or annual; NULL on the free plan

columns.name: mrr_cents
columns.meaning: Monthly recurring revenue in US cents (annual plans divided by 12)

columns.name: ended_at
columns.meaning: When this plan period ended; NULL for the current plan

columns.name: end_reason
columns.meaning: upgrade, downgrade or canceled; NULL for the current plan

tables.name: sessions
tables.grain: One product session by one user.

tables.name: events
tables.grain: One product event as received. Retries can repeat the same event, and some events arrive late.

columns.name: event_id
columns.meaning: Logical event id; repeats when the client retried

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.meaning: When it happened on the client or server (UTC)

columns.name: received_at
columns.meaning: When the pipeline ingested this delivery (UTC)

tables.name: projects
tables.grain: One project created in a workspace.

tables.name: invitations
tables.grain: One invitation sent from a workspace.

columns.name: accepted_at
columns.meaning: Acceptance time; NULL if never accepted

columns.name: accepted_user_id
columns.meaning: User created by accepting; NULL if not accepted

tables.name: experiments
tables.grain: One product experiment.

columns.name: primary_metric
columns.meaning: Event name the experiment aims to increase

columns.name: ended_at
columns.meaning: When the experiment ended; NULL while it is still running

tables.name: experiment_assignments
tables.grain: One user’s assigned experiment variant, recorded the first time they see it.

columns.name: variant
columns.meaning: control, treatment, or variant_b in three-arm tests

tables.name: billing_events
tables.grain: One billing charge or credit for a paid subscription.

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.meaning: US cents; refunds are negative, failed payments record the attempted amount

edgeCases: Retried deliveries with duplicate event_id
Late and out-of-order deliveries (received_at long after occurred_at)
Server-side events with no session
Projects with no creation event
Invitations never accepted; users who joined without an invitation
Referral relationships between users in different workspaces
Cancellations followed by reactivation
Annual and monthly billing; failed payments and partial refunds
Unequal experiment allocation and a three-arm test
Users who never return after signup
qualityNotes: Count logical events with DISTINCT event_id; count deliveries only for pipeline questions.
Use occurred_at for behavior and received_at for ingestion questions.
mrr_cents is list price per month, not cash collected; billing_events records cash.

checks.name: months with signups
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(created_at, 1, 7)) FROM accounts

checks.name: largest account share of events
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events GROUP BY account_id)

checks.name: largest user share of events
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events GROUP BY user_id)

checks.name: event types
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT event_name) FROM events

checks.name: retried deliveries (duplicate event_id)
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) FROM events

checks.name: late deliveries (> 1 hour)
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE julianday(received_at) - julianday(occurred_at) > 1.0 / 24

checks.name: out-of-order deliveries
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events e WHERE occurred_at < (SELECT MAX(occurred_at) FROM events p WHERE p.delivery_id = e.delivery_id - 1)

checks.name: server-side events without session
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE session_id IS NULL

checks.name: one open subscription per account
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts a WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions s WHERE s.account_id = a.account_id AND s.ended_at IS NULL) <> 1

checks.name: accounts that ever paid
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM subscriptions WHERE plan <> 'free'

checks.name: cancellations
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions WHERE end_reason = 'canceled'

checks.name: reactivated accounts
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT account_id FROM subscriptions WHERE plan <> 'free' GROUP BY account_id HAVING SUM(end_reason = 'canceled') > 0 AND COUNT(*) > SUM(end_reason = 'canceled'))

checks.name: paid plan share rises with workspace size
checks.sql: SELECT (SELECT AVG(paid) FROM (SELECT a.account_id, MAX(s.plan <> 'free') AS paid FROM accounts a JOIN subscriptions s USING (account_id) WHERE company_size IN ('201-1000', '1000+') GROUP BY a.account_id)) > (SELECT AVG(paid) FROM (SELECT a.account_id, MAX(s.plan <> 'free') AS paid FROM accounts a JOIN subscriptions s USING (account_id) WHERE company_size = '1-10' GROUP BY a.account_id))

checks.name: invitations never accepted
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invitations WHERE accepted_at IS NULL

checks.name: users joined by domain
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE signup_source = 'domain_join'

checks.name: referred users
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(referred_by_user_id) FROM users

checks.name: projects without creation event
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e WHERE e.event_name = 'project_created' AND e.user_id = p.created_by_user_id AND e.occurred_at = p.created_at)

checks.name: onboarding experiment lift (treatment − control completion rate, pct points)
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(100 * (AVG(CASE WHEN variant = 'treatment' THEN done END) - AVG(CASE WHEN variant = 'control' THEN done END)), 1) FROM (SELECT a.variant, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e WHERE e.user_id = a.user_id AND e.event_name = 'onboarding_completed') AS done FROM experiment_assignments a WHERE a.experiment_id = 1)

checks.name: three-arm experiment variants
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT variant) FROM experiment_assignments a JOIN experiments x USING (experiment_id) WHERE x.experiment_key = 'three_arm_pricing'

checks.name: failed payments
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing_events WHERE event_type = 'payment_failed'

metadata.name: Mobility
metadata.description: A 1-in-87 sample of New York City yellow taxi trips from January–March 2025: pickup and drop-off zones, distances, fares, tips, fees and payment types.

source.publisher: New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC)
source.release: Yellow Taxi Trip Records, January–March 2025 (Parquet); taxi zone lookup table
source.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (free to use, including commercial use, without restriction)
source.attribution: Source: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission, TLC Trip Record Data. Modified by Runtime.
transformations: Deterministic ~1.15% sample of trip records (FNV-1a hash of month and source row number).
extra, mta_tax and improvement_surcharge combined into surcharge_amount; all other amounts kept as recorded.
Timestamps written as NYC local clock time; records outside the file month are kept as published.
Borough names normalised into a boroughs table; code lists from the TLC data dictionary.

reproduction.command: node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> mobility && node datasets/acquire/mobility.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs mobility
reproduction.notes: Committed extracts in datasets/mobility/extract are the build input.

columns.name: borough_name
columns.meaning: Borough label as published by TLC

columns.name: service_zone
columns.meaning: Yellow Zone, Boro Zone, Airports, EWR or N/A

columns.name: is_airport
columns.meaning: 1 for airport zones (service_zone Airports or EWR)

tables.grain: One system that recorded the trip data.

tables.name: payment_types
tables.grain: One way a trip can be paid (for example card or cash).

columns.name: tip_recorded
columns.meaning: 1 when tips are captured in tip_amount (card payments only; cash tips are not recorded)

tables.name: rate_codes
tables.grain: One taxi fare type (for example standard, JFK, or negotiated).

tables.name: calendar
tables.grain: One calendar date in the first quarter of 2025.

tables.name: trips
tables.grain: One yellow taxi trip from January–March 2025.

columns.name: passenger_count
columns.meaning: Driver-entered passengers; NULL when not reported

columns.name: trip_distance_miles
columns.meaning: Taximeter distance in miles; can be 0

columns.name: rate_code_id
columns.meaning: Final rate code; NULL when not reported

columns.name: store_and_fwd_flag
columns.meaning: Y when the record was held in the vehicle before sending

columns.name: fare_amount
columns.meaning: Time-and-distance fare in USD; negative on reversals

columns.name: tip_amount
columns.meaning: Tip in USD; card tips only (cash tips are not recorded)

columns.name: surcharge_amount
columns.meaning: Extra + MTA tax + improvement surcharge, USD

columns.name: cbd_congestion_fee
columns.meaning: MTA Congestion Relief Zone toll (from 2025-01-05), USD

columns.name: total_amount
columns.meaning: Total charged to the passenger excluding cash tips, USD

edgeCases: Flex-fare trips with NULL passenger count and rate code
Negative fares on reversals and disputes
Zero-distance trips
Cash trips record no tip
Unknown and outside-NYC zones
Congestion Relief Zone fee starting 5 January 2025
A pickup timestamp outside the published month
qualityNotes: Cash tips are not recorded, so tip rates should be measured on card trips.
trip_distance_miles is the meter distance, not a straight line between zones.
This is a sample; multiply counts by roughly 87 to estimate citywide volume.

checks.name: pickup dates covered
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(pickup_at, 1, 10)) FROM trips WHERE pickup_at >= '2025-01-01' AND pickup_at < '2025-04-01'

checks.name: largest pickup-zone share
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM trips GROUP BY pickup_zone_id)

checks.name: NULL passenger counts
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE passenger_count IS NULL

checks.name: negative fares
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE fare_amount < 0

checks.name: zero-distance trips
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE trip_distance_miles = 0

checks.name: cash trips
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE payment_type_id = 2

checks.name: congestion relief fees charged
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE cbd_congestion_fee > 0

checks.name: airport pickups

metadata.name: Weather
metadata.description: Three years (2022–2024) of daily observations from 100 NOAA weather stations serving 96 U.S. cities: temperatures, rain, snow and wind.

source.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI); U.S. Census Bureau
source.release: GHCN-Daily via the NCEI Access Data Service (daily-summaries), retrieved 2026-10-14; 2023 Census Gazetteer places
source.attribution: Source: NOAA NCEI Global Historical Climatology Network – Daily (Menne et al., 2012). City coordinates: U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer. Modified by Runtime.
transformations: One first-order station nearest each listed city (within 60 km) with complete TMAX, TMIN and PRCP coverage; extra stations for multi-airport metros.
Seven elements pivoted to one row per station-day, metric units (TAVG is not published for these stations).
Values with a NOAA quality-control flag set to NULL; trace precipitation recorded as 0 mm with precip_trace = 1.
Census regions and divisions, and a 2022–2024 calendar, added by Runtime.

reproduction.command: node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> weather && node datasets/acquire/weather.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs weather
reproduction.notes: The NCEI API serves revised values over time; the committed extract in datasets/weather/extract is the build input.

tables.name: states
tables.grain: One U.S. state or the District of Columbia.

tables.name: cities
tables.grain: One city with weather coverage, including its map location.

columns.name: land_area_sq_mi
columns.meaning: Land area of the incorporated place, square miles

tables.name: stations
tables.grain: One weather station (usually at an airport). A city can have more than one station.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.meaning: 1 for the station nearest the city’s internal point

columns.name: first_observation
columns.meaning: Earliest observation date in this dataset

columns.name: last_observation
columns.meaning: Latest observation date in this dataset

columns.name: reported_days
columns.meaning: Days with at least one reported measurement

tables.name: calendar
tables.grain: One calendar date, 2022–2024.

tables.name: daily_weather
tables.grain: One day of weather for one station. If a station did not report that day, there is no row.

columns.name: precipitation_mm
columns.meaning: Precipitation, mm; 0 with precip_trace = 1 means a trace

columns.name: precip_trace
columns.meaning: 1 when precipitation was a trace (too small to measure)

columns.name: snow_depth_mm
columns.meaning: Snow depth on the ground, mm

edgeCases: Days with no row for a station (gaps in the date series)
Measurements a station does not report at all (snow at southern stations)
Trace precipitation (0 mm but not dry)
Values removed by NOAA quality control
Cities with several stations
Leap day 2024-02-29
Extremes: desert heat, Alaska cold, hurricane rainfall
qualityNotes: NULL means not reported or failed quality control; it is not zero.
Stations represent airports or observation sites, not citywide averages.
Three years are weather, not a climate trend.

checks.name: states covered
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT state_code) FROM cities

checks.name: station-days missing (gaps)
checks.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stations) * 1096 - COUNT(*) FROM daily_weather

checks.name: stations reporting every day
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT station_id FROM daily_weather GROUP BY station_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1096)

checks.name: missing snowfall measurements
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM daily_weather WHERE snowfall_mm IS NULL

checks.name: trace precipitation days
checks.sql: SELECT SUM(precip_trace) FROM daily_weather

checks.name: quality-removed or missing tmax
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM daily_weather WHERE tmax_c IS NULL

metadata.name: Energy
metadata.description: Hourly electricity demand, forecasts, generation and interchange for twelve major U.S. balancing authorities, January–June 2024, with daily fuel mix and flows between neighbouring grids.

source.release: EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor six-month files, 2024 January–June; EIA-930 reference tables
source.attribution: Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor. Modified by Runtime.
transformations: Twelve balancing authorities kept at hourly grain: BPAT, CISO, DUK, ERCO, FPL, ISNE, MISO, NYIS, PJM, SOCO, SWPP, TVA.

metadata.name: Finance / Payments
metadata.description: Six months of a fictional bank: customers, checking, savings and credit-card accounts, cards, merchants, card authorizations and settlements, refunds, disputes and the account ledger.

transformations: Each customer’s accounts are simulated in time order: holds, available balance, declines, settlements, overdrafts and refunds follow from the running balance.
Payroll, rent, utilities, subscriptions, savings transfers, card payments and interest recur on realistic schedules.
Merchant category codes follow ISO 18245; names, people and amounts are fictional.

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

columns.meaning: Merchant request id; a retried request reuses it

columns.meaning: Requested amount in the transaction currency

columns.name: currency
columns.meaning: USD, EUR, GBP, CAD or MXN

columns.name: decline_reason
columns.meaning: insufficient_funds, credit_limit, suspected_fraud, expired_card or card_frozen; NULL when approved

tables.grain: One cardholder dispute against a settlement.

columns.name: transaction_type
columns.meaning: Kind of money movement (purchase, refund, transfer, fee, and similar)

columns.name: posted_at
columns.meaning: When it reached the ledger; NULL while pending or after reversal

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.meaning: Merchant for card and bill entries

edgeCases: Declines for insufficient funds, credit limit, fraud, frozen and expired cards
Duplicate approvals from network retries (shared request_key) that never settle
Settled amounts different from authorized amounts (tips, fuel, hotels, currency)
Merchant voids (reversed) and purchases still pending at the end of the period
Partial and multiple refunds; disputes credited, rejected or open
Overdrafts and overdraft fees
Recurring charges with mid-period price increases
Lost cards replaced on the same account
Settlements with no ledger posting and manual ledger adjustments
qualityNotes: All money is integer US cents except authorization amounts, which are in the transaction currency.
Authorizations are requests, not money movement; only posted ledger entries change balances.
Balance at time t = opening_balance_cents + SUM(amount_cents) of posted entries with posted_at <= t.

metadata.name: Healthcare
metadata.description: Three years of synthetic patient journeys: patients, clinicians, appointments, visits, diagnoses, prescriptions, vital signs, lab results and procedures. No real person’s health information is present.

source.attribution: Synthetic data generated by Runtime. Diagnosis codes are ICD-10-CM (U.S. public domain); procedure and measurement codes are Runtime-defined.
transformations: Age and frailty drive chronic-condition prevalence; conditions drive follow-up visits, labs and medications.
Chronic medications are 180-day supplies renewed early (overlapping intervals) or late (gaps in therapy).
Appointments can be cancelled and rebooked, missed (no-show) or still scheduled after the data ends.
Emergency visits can lead to inpatient stays and 30-day readmissions.
Modeled after the concepts of Synthea; no Synthea output or real patient data is used.

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

edgeCases: Patients with no encounters; providers who never saw a patient
Cancelled, no-show and future-scheduled appointments with no encounter
Overlapping and gapped medication fill intervals
Ongoing chronic conditions with NULL resolved dates
Measurements attempted but not obtained (NULL value)
Inpatient stays spanning several days; 30-day readmissions
Patients who died during the period
Telehealth visits without vital signs
qualityNotes: All people and clinicians are fictional; prevalence and costs are illustrative, not epidemiological estimates.
stop_date is exclusive: a fill covers start_date up to the day before stop_date.
Use the patient’s age at the visit, not today, for age-based analysis.

metadata.name: IoT / Sensors
metadata.description: Two months of telemetry from sensors across eight fictional facilities: cold rooms, freezers, production lines, offices and pump stations, with alerts, outages and maintenance.

transformations: Signals follow physical patterns: defrost cycles, occupancy-driven CO2, working-hours power, vibration drift before failures, battery discharge.
Alerts are derived from the readings with hysteresis; status events and maintenance follow outages and failures.
Network outages buffer readings and deliver them late; power outages lose them; about 1% of messages are retransmitted.

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

tables.name: locations
tables.grain: One monitored zone inside a site.

columns.name: zone_name
columns.meaning: Room or area within the site

columns.name: timezone
columns.meaning: IANA time zone of the site

tables.grain: One kind of measurement (for example temperature), including valid ranges and alert thresholds.

columns.name: alert_low
columns.meaning: Alert when the value falls below this; NULL if no low threshold

columns.name: alert_high
columns.meaning: Alert when the value rises above this; NULL if no high threshold

tables.grain: One installed sensor device.

columns.name: firmware_version
columns.meaning: Firmware at the end of the period

columns.name: retired_at
columns.meaning: Removal time; NULL while in service

tables.name: sensor_readings
tables.grain: One sensor reading. The same reading can arrive more than once when a device retransmits.

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.meaning: Measurement time on the device clock (UTC)

columns.name: received_at
columns.meaning: Platform ingestion time (UTC); late when the device buffered offline

columns.name: value
columns.meaning: Measured value in the type’s unit; NULL when the sensor reported a fault

columns.name: battery_pct
columns.meaning: Battery level for battery-powered devices; NULL for mains-powered

columns.name: gateway_id
columns.meaning: Wireless gateway that relayed the reading; NULL for wired (mains-powered) devices

columns.name: signal_rssi_dbm
columns.meaning: Received signal strength at the gateway, dBm (closer to 0 is stronger); NULL for wired devices

columns.name: quality_flag
columns.meaning: Platform check on arrival: ok, out_of_range (outside the sensor type’s valid range) or fault (no value)

tables.grain: One alert period when a device went out of range or lost connectivity.

columns.name: opened_at
columns.meaning: First reading or check that triggered the alert

columns.name: closed_at
columns.meaning: When the condition cleared; NULL if still open

columns.name: peak_value
columns.meaning: Most extreme value while open; NULL for connectivity alerts

tables.name: maintenance
tables.grain: One maintenance visit for a device. Two technicians can log overlapping orders for the same visit.

columns.name: maintenance_type
columns.meaning: calibration, battery_replacement, repair, firmware_update or replacement

columns.name: completed_at
columns.meaning: Work end; NULL if still open

tables.name: device_status_events
tables.grain: One change in a device’s status. That status lasts until the next status event.

columns.name: status
columns.meaning: online, offline, degraded, maintenance or retired

edgeCases: Gaps in readings during outages and dropped messages
Late batches delivered after a network outage (received_at ≫ recorded_at)
Retransmitted duplicates with the same sequence_number
Fault readings: NULL values and physically impossible values
Threshold violations forming consecutive runs (islands)
Overlapping maintenance work orders for the same device
Devices installed or retired during the period; spares that never reported
Status changes recorded only when the state changes (fill-forward needed)
qualityNotes: Order by recorded_at for physical analysis and by received_at for pipeline analysis.
Deduplicate on (device_id, sequence_number) before counting readings.
Exclude values outside the sensor type’s valid range before averaging.

checks.name: NULL fault readings

metadata.name: Logistics
metadata.description: Four months of a fictional parcel network: shipments and packages moving from fulfillment centers through sortation hubs to delivery stations, with every scan, delivery attempt and return.

transformations: Each package follows a physical path: pickup, origin departure, one or two hubs, delivery station, out for delivery, attempts.
About 5% of intermediate scans are missing, 3.5% of scanner events repeat, carrier API events arrive in delayed batches.
Failed attempts are retried on business days; three failures, a refusal or damage return the package to sender.
Shipper names, tracking numbers and postal codes are entered inconsistently on purpose.

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

edgeCases: Duplicate scans of the same step
Missing intermediate scans
Late, batched and out-of-order ingestion (recorded_at)
A scan recorded after delivery (out_for_delivery after delivered)
Reroutes to a different delivery station
Failed attempts, returns to sender and lost packages
Packages still in transit at the end of the data
Messy shipper names, tracking numbers and postal codes
qualityNotes: The latest state of a package is its most recent event by event_at, not by event_id.
Normalize tracking numbers with UPPER and REPLACE before matching.
promised_delivery_date counts business days from label creation.

checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tracking_events WHERE exception_code IS NOT NULL AND event_type NOT IN ('exception', 'rerouted', 'returned_to_sender')

checks.name: largest package share of events
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM tracking_events GROUP BY package_id)

checks.name: duplicate scans
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_events GROUP BY package_id, event_type, warehouse_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 AND event_type NOT IN ('out_for_delivery', 'delivery_failed', 'warehouse_arrival', 'warehouse_departure'))

checks.name: repeated scanner events within 15 minutes
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT package_id, event_type, event_at, LAG(event_at) OVER (PARTITION BY package_id, event_type, warehouse_id ORDER BY event_at) AS prev FROM tracking_events) WHERE (julianday(event_at) - julianday(prev)) * 1440 <= 15

checks.name: late ingestion (> 1 hour)
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tracking_events WHERE julianday(recorded_at) - julianday(event_at) > 1.0 / 24

checks.name: out-of-order ingestion within a package
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT event_at, LAG(event_at) OVER (PARTITION BY package_id ORDER BY recorded_at, event_id) AS prev FROM tracking_events) WHERE event_at < prev

checks.name: packages with failed attempts
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT package_id) FROM delivery_attempts WHERE outcome <> 'delivered'

checks.name: returned packages
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT package_id) FROM tracking_events WHERE event_type = 'returned_to_sender'

checks.name: rerouted packages
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT package_id) FROM tracking_events WHERE event_type = 'rerouted'

checks.name: packages never delivered
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM packages p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracking_events e WHERE e.package_id = p.package_id AND e.event_type = 'delivered')

checks.name: messy tracking numbers
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM packages WHERE tracking_number <> UPPER(REPLACE(tracking_number, ' ', ''))

checks.name: postal codes needing repair
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments WHERE destination_postal_code IS NULL OR length(destination_postal_code) <> 5

checks.name: shipper name variants
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT UPPER(TRIM(REPLACE(shipper_name, '  ', ' ')))) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT shipper_name FROM shipments)

checks.name: driver notes
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(driver_note) FROM delivery_attempts

metadata.name: Developer Platform
metadata.description: Eighteen months of activity on a fictional code-hosting platform: organizations, nested teams, developers and managers, repositories and forks, pull requests, reviews, commits, issues, deployments and incidents.

transformations: Organizations have nested teams (up to four levels) and a management chain from VP to engineers.
Repository activity drives pull requests; reviewers come from the owning team; merged PRs advance the commit chain and can be deployed.
Rolled-back production deployments can open incidents; other incidents have no deployment cause.

reproduction.notes: Generator version 3.0.0; deterministic for a given seed.

tables.name: organizations
tables.grain: One customer organization on the developer platform.

tables.name: teams
tables.grain: One team inside an organization. Teams can nest under other teams.

columns.name: parent_team_id
columns.meaning: Parent team; NULL for top-level teams

tables.name: developers
tables.grain: One person with an account in an organization.

columns.name: team_id
columns.meaning: Primary team; NULL for people not assigned to a team

columns.name: role
columns.meaning: engineer, senior_engineer, staff_engineer, manager, director, vp or contractor

columns.name: manager_id
columns.meaning: Manager; NULL at the top of an organization

tables.name: repositories
tables.grain: One code repository. Forks point to the repository they were copied from.

columns.name: owning_team_id
columns.meaning: Owning team; NULL when ownership is unassigned

columns.name: forked_from_repository_id
columns.meaning: Source repository for forks; NULL otherwise

tables.name: pull_requests
tables.grain: One pull request.

columns.name: closed_at
columns.meaning: Closed or merged; NULL while open

tables.name: commits
tables.grain: One code commit. Each commit can point to the previous commit on its branch.

columns.name: author_id
columns.meaning: Author; NULL for commits by unlinked emails and bots

columns.name: pull_request_id
columns.meaning: Pull request it belongs to; NULL for direct pushes

columns.name: parent_sha
columns.meaning: Parent commit; NULL for a repository’s first commit

columns.name: message
columns.meaning: First line of the commit message

tables.name: reviews
tables.grain: One review submitted on a pull request.

tables.name: issues
tables.grain: One tracked issue.

tables.name: deployments
tables.grain: One deployment of a commit to an environment.

columns.name: triggered_by_id
columns.meaning: Who triggered it; NULL for automated deploys

tables.name: incidents
tables.grain: One production incident.

columns.name: deployment_id
columns.meaning: Deployment identified as the cause; NULL when not caused by a deploy

edgeCases: Team hierarchy up to four levels; management chains of different depth
Developers with no team; repositories with no owning team
Forks referencing their source repository
Commits with no linked author (bots, unlinked emails) and direct pushes without a PR
Pull requests with no reviews, several reviews, or changes requested then approved
Open pull requests and issues at the end of the data
Failed and rolled-back deployments; incidents with and without a deployment cause
Developers who left during the period
qualityNotes: Review time is measured from pull_requests.created_at to the first review’s submitted_at.
A developer can author and review in the same repository but never reviews their own pull request.
Deployment frequency and change failure rate are computed on production deployments.

checks.name: months with pull requests
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(created_at, 1, 7)) FROM pull_requests

checks.name: largest repository share of PRs
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM pull_requests GROUP BY repository_id)

checks.name: team hierarchy depth ≥ 3
checks.sql: WITH RECURSIVE d(team_id, depth) AS (SELECT team_id, 1 FROM teams WHERE parent_team_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT t.team_id, d.depth + 1 FROM teams t JOIN d ON t.parent_team_id = d.team_id) SELECT MAX(depth) FROM d

checks.name: management chain depth ≥ 4
checks.sql: WITH RECURSIVE m(developer_id, depth) AS (SELECT developer_id, 1 FROM developers WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT d.developer_id, m.depth + 1 FROM developers d JOIN m ON d.manager_id = m.developer_id) SELECT MAX(depth) FROM m

checks.name: forks
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(forked_from_repository_id) FROM repositories

checks.name: commits without author
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM commits WHERE author_id IS NULL

checks.name: direct pushes
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM commits WHERE pull_request_id IS NULL

checks.name: PRs without reviews
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pull_requests p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.pull_request_id = p.pull_request_id)

checks.name: self-reviews
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reviews r JOIN pull_requests p USING (pull_request_id) WHERE r.reviewer_id = p.author_id

checks.name: mutual reviewer pairs
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT p.author_id AS a, r.reviewer_id AS b FROM reviews r JOIN pull_requests p USING (pull_request_id)) x WHERE x.a < x.b AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r2 JOIN pull_requests p2 USING (pull_request_id) WHERE p2.author_id = x.b AND r2.reviewer_id = x.a)

checks.name: deployment statuses
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT status) FROM deployments

checks.name: incidents caused by deployments
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(deployment_id) FROM incidents

checks.name: incidents without deployment cause
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE deployment_id IS NULL

checks.name: developers who left
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(left_at) FROM developers

checks.name: unassigned developers
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM developers WHERE team_id IS NULL

metadata.name: Sports
metadata.description: Ten seasons of Major League Baseball results (2016–2025) with every 2025 player batting line, rosters, ballparks and month-end standings.

source.release: Retrosheet CSV downloads: gameinfo (1897–2025), 2025 season files, biographical files
source.license: Retrosheet notice: free use including commercial products, provided the Retrosheet statement appears prominently
source.attribution: The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at "www.retrosheet.org".
transformations: Regular-season and postseason games 2016–2025; All-Star games excluded.
2025 batting lines with stattype = value; a player re-entering one game is summed to one line.
Players are all 2025 roster entries; primary position is the position with the most 2025 games.
League and division assignments, the Rays nickname and venue countries added by Runtime.
Seasons and month-end standings derived from game results.

reproduction.command: node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> sports && node datasets/acquire/sports.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs sports
reproduction.notes: Committed extracts in datasets/sports/extract are the build input.

tables.name: teams
tables.grain: One MLB team. The Athletics appear twice: Oakland (OAK) through 2024, then Sacramento (ATH) in 2025.

columns.name: franchise_id
columns.meaning: Franchise code; OAK and ATH share one franchise

tables.name: venues
tables.grain: One ballpark that hosted a game, including neutral and international sites.

columns.name: region
columns.meaning: U.S. state code, or country/territory for sites outside the 50 states

tables.name: seasons
tables.grain: One MLB season.

columns.name: games_per_team
columns.meaning: Scheduled regular-season games per team (60 in 2020)

tables.name: games
tables.grain: One completed regular-season or postseason game.

columns.name: game_id
columns.meaning: Retrosheet game id: home team, date and game number

columns.name: game_number
columns.meaning: 0 for a single game, 1 or 2 for doubleheaders

columns.name: game_type
columns.meaning: regular, playoff (tiebreaker), wildcard, divisionseries, lcs or worldseries

columns.name: home_score
columns.meaning: Runs scored by the home club

columns.name: away_score
columns.meaning: Runs scored by the visiting club

columns.name: attendance
columns.meaning: Paid attendance; NULL when not reported (most 2020 games had no fans)

tables.name: players
tables.grain: One player who appeared in a 2025 MLB game.

columns.name: primary_position
columns.meaning: Position with the most 2025 games (P, C, 1B … DH)

tables.name: player_game_stats
tables.grain: One player’s batting stats in one 2025 game. Pitchers usually appear with zero plate appearances.

columns.name: batting_order
columns.meaning: Lineup slot 1–9; NULL for some substitutes

columns.name: started
columns.meaning: 1 for the starting player in the lineup slot

tables.name: standings
tables.grain: One team’s win–loss record at the end of a month (and at season end).

edgeCases: A relocated franchise with two team codes (OAK → ATH)
The shortened 60-game 2020 season played mostly without fans (NULL attendance)
Doubleheaders on the same date
Neutral and international sites (London, Tokyo, Seoul, Mexico City, Field of Dreams)
Pitchers with batting lines of zero plate appearances
Ties in wins, runs and player totals
Substitutes without a recorded lineup slot
qualityNotes: Player batting lines cover 2025 only; game results cover ten seasons.
Standings are cumulative to each snapshot date; differences between snapshots give monthly records.
A team appears in two rows per game in player_game_stats joins only through its own players.

checks.name: seasons with games
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT season) FROM games

checks.name: 2020 short season games
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND game_type = 'regular'

checks.name: doubleheader games
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games WHERE game_number > 0

checks.name: postseason games
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games WHERE game_type <> 'regular'

checks.name: games without attendance
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games WHERE attendance IS NULL

checks.name: international or neutral venues
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM venues WHERE country <> 'United States'

checks.name: relocated franchise codes
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM teams WHERE franchise_id = 'OAK'

checks.name: players who never batted (zero plate appearances)
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_id FROM player_game_stats GROUP BY player_id HAVING SUM(plate_appearances) = 0)

checks.name: largest player share of lines
checks.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(n) * 1.0 / SUM(n), 4) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM player_game_stats GROUP BY player_id)

checks.name: season-end standings rows
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM standings s JOIN seasons x ON x.season = s.season AND s.as_of_date = x.last_regular_date

checks.name: players tied on 2025 home runs
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT SUM(home_runs) AS hr FROM player_game_stats GROUP BY player_id) GROUP BY hr HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

contract.name: players who never batted (zero plate appearances)
